title: Harry Styles Appears to Reveal the Date He Finished ‘Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally’
summary: The pop star seems to have had the LP waiting in the tank for several months.
contentText:
Harry Styles ‘ latest album is brand new for fans, but for him, it may be several months old.

Related

Harry Styles Is Ready to ‘Go to Work’ in Thrilling ‘One Night in Manchester’ Trailer

On Friday (March 6), the day of Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally ‘s release, the pop star shared a carousel of photos on Instagram from the process of recording and producing the LP. Some of the snaps show Styles hard at work in the studio with his collaborators, and others show the singer directing a group of backup vocalists or marked-up sheet music.

And one pic appeared to reveal the day Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally was finished: June 25, 2025, as scrawled in what appears to be Styles’ handwriting next to the words “LP4 complete.”

“It’s all waiting there for you,” Styles wrote in the caption.

It wouldn’t be for more than half a year after June 25 when fans finally got their hands on the LP, which features 12 tracks (including Billboard Hot 100 -topping lead single “Aperture”). The album marks a distinct sonic change for Styles, who explores the realm of dance music throughout the project.

Styles is now gearing up for his one-night-only show at the Co-op Live in Manchester, England, on the evening of Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally ‘s release, a show that Netflix will film and premiere as a concert film on Sunday (March 8). It’ll give fans a taste of what’s to come on the Grammy winner’s Together, Together tour, which will involve more than 60 shows across seven venues, including 30 nights at Madison Square Garden in New York City and 12 at Wembley Stadium in London.

“I think it makes the show better,” Styles explained of the mini-residency approach in a recent interview with Zane Lowe. “I think you can build something that doesn’t have to travel every night. I think there’s something in this that allows me to, like, stay in my life while I’m doing it. And therefore I think [it] allows me to take care of myself better, which I think makes me better at doing the thing.”
